operations.comment: ; Symbols identify physical hardware registers or mechanically established RAM roles.
; Zero-page shared fields are overlays: animation/menu/gameplay reuse the same bytes.
; Work15..Work23 and Sharedxx are caller-owned temporaries, never persistent game fields.
; Object arrays have 25 slots for update dispatch; collision scans use slots 0..23.
; Packed object flags: bit 7 active, bits 2..6 type, low two bits direction.
; RoomTiles is a 16x16 byte grid; positions are pixels, one cell per sixteen pixels.
; OamBuffer holds 64 four-byte NES sprite records. PpuQueue is a byte-indexed ring.
; Numeric ROM operands retain unnamed table slices or base-before-slice views; they do not change physical byte classification.
; iNES header: signature, PRG/CHR sizes and mapper fields. Keep all sixteen bytes unchanged.
; Clear the active mask, shared scroll deltas/fractions and eight duration counters. The adjacent initializer consumes counted inline stream roots and allocates free animation slots.

; Remove the CPU return address and read N followed by N little-endian stream pointers. Continue at return+2+2*N; allocate free slots with separate RAM VM-stack origins. This contract requires N=1..8 and initialized scene storage; no free slot jumps directly to the computed continuation.
; Advance the shared 16-bit tick, update eight active animation slots, then integrate signed fractional scrolling. The same zero-page workspace is reused by gameplay elsewhere.
; Carry the tick into its high byte.
; The active mask chooses eight slots. Each slot interprets a nibble-coded stream, updates fractional positions and renders unless its image is $ff.
; Extend a negative horizontal delta through the high coordinate byte.
; Add fractional horizontal and vertical deltas; vertical wrapping uses 240 scanlines per nametable.
; Correct the 256-byte carry to the 240-line vertical period.
; Save vertical position. The second entry handles a negative vertical delta by subtracting its magnitude.
; Correct vertical underflow and decrement the nametable coordinate.
; Store wrapped vertical position. A separate entry loads animation slot pointers, signed velocities, fractional positions and countdowns; commands dispatch through a RAM pointer.
; Load and advance one active animation slot.
; Clear this slot in the active mask when its stream reaches zero.
; Small command bytes select one pointer table; high-nibble commands also load a duration from the low nibble. Both call the pointer trampoline and resume the slot.
; Split handler arrays: nine small-command low bytes, nine high bytes, ten timed-command low bytes and ten high bytes. Dispatch is bounded to those independently established domains.

; Push the next stream position and repetition count onto this slot's RAM stack. The adjacent loop-end entry decrements the count, restores the cursor on repetition, or drops the saved frame when exhausted.
; Decrement the saved loop count. Zero discards the frame and advances; otherwise restore the saved stream cursor.
; Read two successive stream bytes into the current stream pointer, low byte first.

; Read a destination, push the return cursor on the slot's RAM stack and switch streams. Adjacent entries return from a stream call, set a slot duration, select music or request an effect. These are VM commands, separate from CPU return frames.
; Pop the saved stream cursor from the slot RAM stack.
; Copy the next stream byte to this slot duration and advance.
; Read a music ID, submit it and advance.
; Read an effect ID, submit it and advance.
; Separate command entries set image ID, integer position or signed packed velocities from the stream. The final stream read advances past each payload.
; Read integer X/Y and clear packed fractional coordinates.
; Read two signed 4.4 slot velocities and split each into fractional and sign-extended integer fields.

; Decode signed 4.4 X/Y increments and add them to slot velocity. Following command entries set scroll position, set or add signed scroll deltas, then update a four-color palette from three arguments: slot, pointer low, pointer high.
; Read horizontal low/page then vertical low/page scroll coordinates.
; Read and add signed 4.4 horizontal/vertical deltas to the shared scroll motion.
; Read slot first, then pointer low/high. The three arguments become Y,A,X for the four-color copy; corrected palette sources lie at physical $2445/$2449/$244D.
; Add stream-provided byte offsets to the slot position, wrapping at 256.

; Read a low/high palette pointer and copy sixteen colors. The following callback command reads a low/high CPU pointer, advances the stream, then tail jumps to it. Only the established finite scene callback set has a balanced return contract.
; Read the callback pointer, advance once beyond it and tail jump; only the initialized finite callback closure is summarized.
; Advance the 16-bit stream cursor before reading at Y; callers normally keep Y zero.
; Carry cursor increment into the high byte.
; Return the indexed stream byte. Another entry splits a packed signed 4.4 displacement into fractional A and sign-extended integer X.
; A packed signed 4.4 delta returns fraction in A and signed integer in X.
; Eight clear masks followed by eight set masks; bit X selects one of the eight animation slots.
; Select 8x16 sprites and the background pattern page, initialize display resources, then run the intro/title sequence.
; Run title-choice setup, then continue to the tutorial and shared menu cycle.
; Run the scripted tutorial before entering the shared menu setup.
; Run the attract/title setup before the menu screen; both calls return under the initialized scene contract.
; Run the title-choice screen, then repeat the title cycle.
; Run menu setup and join the tutorial/title cycle.
; Enter the tutorial setup. The separate display initializer chooses a CHR register and clears/loads nametable data through inline descriptor transfers.
; Select display CHR state and clear/load the nametable before the title resource setup.
; Little-endian inline PPU descriptor pointer $8437; the JSR consumer adjusts its stacked return by two. This CPU execution view is not a physical ROM identity.
; Restore rendering, load resource set eight, reset scroll, wait thirty frames and load the title palette with signed brightness before timed fade/wait steps.

; PPU descriptor/source bytes: destination low/high and width/height precede the source. Ordinary mode reads width*height payload bytes; repeated mode reuses one byte. The accepted consumer mode and exact physical region delimit this record.
; NES palette bytes in four-color groups. The palette copy consumer supplies group selection/brightness; exact scene ownership is not inferred from color patterns alone.
; Enable the interrupt-level Start/Select escape and begin a palette transition. This appears to be a title/attract setup path.
; Prepare the display and fade in, enable interrupt escape, then initialize animation slots from the following counted roots.
; Counted animation roots: N=3, followed by 3 little-endian stream pointers ($849E, $84BB, $848E). The initializer resumes beyond this payload; pointers apply only to initialized slot/stack storage.
; Wait, build OAM and tick animation with stable sprite order until tick low reaches $D2; disable interrupt escape and transfer the next display.

; Use the more restrictive pushing tile rules before object overlap checks.
; Apply the pushing tile ranges to the second leading tile.
; Return blocked with original probe arguments restored.

; Preserve the sampled tile pair across the generic probe, then apply special rail/floor tile compatibility. Return carry for blocking, Y for the movement subtype, and restore the current probe slot/direction.

; Direction-indexed leading probe offsets and matching boundary comparison values.
; Draw image A at object slot X's current position. Tail call clobbers X/Y as the sprite renderer does.

; Only reconsider direction at eight-pixel alignment. Use a packed two-bit direction history or compare player axes to try available routes; remember failed routes, reverse if necessary, update packed direction and target. Carry follows the shared probe contract.
; Four clear masks followed by four set masks update packed direction history without changing other bits.

; Push a two-bit choice into ObjectAux and increment the low two-bit history depth in ObjectTimer. Adjacent entries pop a choice or derive horizontal/vertical preferred directions toward the player, retaining prior preference at equal coordinates.
; Shift the two-bit history and increment its low depth field.
; Return the latest two-bit direction while reducing depth.
; Compute horizontal/vertical preferences, retaining encoded prior choices at equal coordinates.
; Begin path-interaction checks when object and player X differ by at most one pixel.
; Form a narrow object-centered X interval and a vertical span to the player's target, then scan blocking objects.
; On a clear probe set direction down, derive the row distance to player target and test the vertical grid path; failed searches take the shared fallback.
; Construct the opposite vertical span and test for blocking objects.
; On a clear probe set direction up, derive the row distance to player target and scan backward through grid cells.
; Require near-equal Y, construct a horizontal span to the player's target and reject intervening objects.
; Compute room-cell endpoints for a rightward path.
; Compute column distance to player target, scan forward through cells and join the successful direction path.
; Test the leftward span, derive tile endpoints and scan the intervening cells backward; successful continuation repeats the action check.
; Save direction three and request sound seven before creating the slot-zero player-capture object.

; Restore the selected direction and build slot zero with a player-relative target and source-object position. Choose packed type from source class, set state one and activate the player override/pause flags.
; Restore the current object slot before returning.
; Four player-relative X and four Y target deltas for the slot-zero capture object.
; Convert object position and its direction-offset neighbor into cell indices saved in two scratch bytes.
; Direction-selected X/Y step bytes used by the bounded grid-path helper.
; Scan 24 active objects below state five; test target coordinates against half-open scratch X/Y bounds and return carry set if any overlap.
; Carry clear reports that the bounded tile path has no disallowed cells.
; Carry set reports a blocked path. An adjacent entry begins boss activity/countdown selection.
; Dispatch boss movement or clear countdown.
; Count down the boss-clear delay; expiration sets room clear and updates the exit tile, while intermediate frames select boss poses.
; Route to the shared boss pose entry.

; Every 32 object frames, while the boss is high enough, find an inactive slot and begin initializing its position.
; Set projectile Y relative to boss Y, clear fractional/target fields, activate packed type $20 facing down and request the spawn effect.
; Accelerate horizontally and vertically toward fixed thresholds, then integrate two signed fractional coordinates.
; Select bobbing offset from frame phase; an active countdown chooses a temporary palette effect.
; Decrement effect countdown, select alternate palette source and copy its four-byte group.
; Select tile $3A and join the shared boss tile-change path.
; Draw two image components with frame-based animation at boss coordinates; second component is 48 pixels lower.
; Boss tile/image-like byte patterns include the indexed tile delta origin used by the boss update. Remaining semantic subdivisions are uncertain; no codec or full selector domain is asserted.

; Use RAM $06F1/$06F2 as scene countdowns, alternating palettes and frame rendering; increase the delay near the end, draw boss/player images and return when the main countdown reaches zero. These addresses overlay object storage during this initialized scene.
; NES palette bytes in four-color groups. The palette copy consumer supplies group selection/brightness; exact scene ownership is not inferred from color patterns alone.
; Tail-call the handler pointer in the shared zero-page pointer; caller's JSR supplies the return address.

; Preserve X/Y and replace one two-bit quadrant at RAM pointer $0343+((Y&$FC)*2)+((X&$1C)>>2), bounded by $0542. The following standalone helper divides unsigned A/X into decimal digits through repeated subtraction of 10000/1000/100/10.
; Treat X:A as unsigned sixteen bits, repeatedly subtract four decimal divisors and write quotient digits to Work15..Work18; Work19/Work1A retain the remainder.
; High bytes then low bytes of unsigned divisors 10000,1000,100,10; the standalone decimal helper compares/subtracts each divisor.
; Compute the attribute byte and quadrant, shift a two-bit value into position, preserve other quadrants and queue one PPU byte.
; Shift the attribute value by two bits for each quadrant offset.
; Mask the prior quadrant, merge the new value and submit the changed attribute byte.
; Little-endian inline PPU descriptor pointer $016C; the JSR consumer adjusts its stacked return by two. This CPU execution view is not a physical ROM identity.
; Restore the caller's tile X/Y coordinates from the stack.

; Submit a repeated-data clear descriptor through its inline pointer.

; Submit the second repeated-data clear descriptor.

; Subtract the selected brightness step; underflow becomes black $0f.

; Describe a 32-byte transfer to PPU palette $3f00 and call the inline-parameter transfer entry.
; Little-endian inline PPU descriptor pointer $016A; the JSR consumer adjusts its stacked return by two. This CPU execution view is not a physical ROM identity.
; Return after the inline transfer payload.
; Five indexed brightness adjustment values used by the palette conversion routine.
; Changed held input is emitted immediately; unchanged input waits twelve ticks then repeats every six ticks using a high-bit timer.
; Publish the new held input and restart the repeat delay.
; Advance the repeat timer and test first/repeat thresholds.
; Publish held input and reload the repeat phase at $80.
; Publish no command between repeat ticks.
; Split A into horizontal bit zero and vertical upper bits; clear fine X/Y scroll.
; Wait X video frames; X zero wraps to 256 iterations.
; Save the outer group count and begin a sixty-frame inner delay.
; Restore and decrement outer count, then repeat or return.
; Toggle OAM insertion order each frame, select the cursor endpoint, and hide reserved sprite entries with Y=$f0.
; Two choices read by the sprite-order setup helper.
; Hide unused OAM entries in the current insertion direction. A second entry draws image A at X/Y, choosing variable or fixed-size image format.
; Draw image A at pixel coordinates X/Y; select variable or fixed two-sprite format.
; Extend Y minus one into its high/clipping bit.
; Look up the image record, read its component count, then consume signed Y offset, tile, attribute and signed X offset per sprite; clipping checks the high coordinate bits.
; Skip the remaining fields for a vertically clipped component.
; Write tile/attribute and compute signed X offset, suppressing horizontally clipped components.
; Keep the OAM cursor unchanged for a clipped component.
; Complete X/clipping check and move the cursor forward or backward by four bytes according to frame order.
; Skip the clipped sprite's tile, attribute and X fields.
; Iterate components, store OAM cursor and clear clipping extensions. A separate entry handles fixed two-sprite records: four bytes per image, attributes XORed with a shared flip mask.
; Draw a fixed pair of sprites from a four-byte image record.
; Horizontal offsets eight and zero, read with X=2 then 1 from base CPU $CEC0. That base is an RTS; exactly the following two bytes are data.
; Run eleven feedback-shift rounds on the two-byte random state, preserve X and return its low byte. Exact polynomial intent is unresolved.

; Decode the stream at RAM pointer $7D/$7E to PPU address $81/$82. $FF terminates; short/extended counts drive literal, repeated, alternating or incrementing writes. Copy modes read PPU data into $0300, optionally reverse bit order or byte order, then write it back. Source/destination/count scratch overlays gameplay fields; this routine runs in display setup with rendering/NMI controlled by its caller.
; Entry takes compressed source $7D/$7E and destination $81/$82; these RAM fields overlay gameplay state.
; Choose the low-byte count for the last chunk, or zero for a full 256-byte chunk; store it for read/write helpers.
; Prime buffered PPUDATA at the copy source and read a chunk into RAM $0300 indexed backwards.
; Write the buffered chunk to the destination and advance the PPU destination across the chunk.
; Reverse each buffered byte through eight shifts, preserving the chunk indexing.
; Back up the PPU source by the selected count, prime the read buffer and populate the chunk in the reverse byte order.
; Clear the PPUCTRL NMI bit in hardware and its shadow.
; Set bit seven in the PPU control shadow and join the shared hardware-write tail.
; Preserve A; with NMI enabled wait on the interrupt handshake, otherwise poll PPUSTATUS for a fresh vblank.
; Wait for vblank to end and then begin; restore saved A.
; Wait for a frame with A zero, clear PPUMASK and queue mode. The adjacent restore entry uses the saved mask, then reapplies scroll.
; Use PpuMaskShadow, perform the shared frame/mask update and restore scroll.
; Select repeated-source transfer mode. Calls embed a two-byte descriptor pointer after JSR; the callee adjusts the stacked return address past it.
; Select direct attribute mode. Adjacent entry selects advancing-source mode; common setup captures A/X/Y and the inline descriptor pointer while advancing the return address by two.
; Read an inline descriptor pointer after JSR and skip it in the stacked return address.
; Carry the adjusted return pointer into its high byte.
; Restore the adjusted return address. Descriptor begins destination low/high, width and height, then payload. Direct mode uses preloaded dimensions; shape selects row versus column traversal.
; Save PPUCTRL and disable NMI before writing the row directly to PPUDATA, then restore control and advance to the next row.
; Write a row directly to PPUDATA with the shadow PPU increment mode. Repeated-source mode retains its byte; ordinary sources advance. Restore NMI control and join the shared row completion.
; Begin a queue record with destination and width, emit width bytes and optionally advance the source, then commit the record.
; Finish the row record, advance destination by 32 and repeat height times; restore the caller's A/X/Y on completion.
; Set the vertical-increment destination flag, preserve width and source, and choose immediate or queued transfer path.
; Set PPU increment 32 and write a column, advancing source by width unless repeated mode. Restore NMI control and join column completion.
; Reserve queue capacity before appending the column count and payload and publishing the record.

; Queue a column's length and bytes, publish the record, advance destination and restore the saved source for the next column. Shared completion restores A/X/Y. The following independent entry discards queued work by copying tail to head.
; Discard pending records by copying queue tail to head.
; Compare circular queue occupancy against $40 before reserving another record; frame wait allows NMI to drain it.
; Wait one frame, then retry the bounded queue-space calculation.
; Retry the existing queue-space calculation after the intervening wait/service.

; Store destination high/low at queue head and return a private write cursor. Other entries append A, commit cursor, drain bounded records during NMI, and serially read controllers. High destination bit selects PPU increment 32; each record has a count followed by payload.
; Append A at the private queue cursor without publishing the record.
; Publish the private cursor as queue head.
; Drain complete queue records during NMI, bounded by a byte budget.
; Latch both controllers and read their serial bits.
; Read eight serial bits, combine compatible low input lines and compute newly pressed bits.
; Fill all 256 bytes of OamBuffer with $F0, hiding sprites by their Y fields; this also overwrites the other sprite fields.
; Continue clearing OAM entries until X wraps, then return.
; Save CPU registers, DMA OAM from page four, apply pending PPUMASK, drain transfers, update scroll/CHR/controller/audio and set the frame handshake.

; Restore Y/X/A and return from interrupt. A separate entry installs nametable bits and scroll registers from shared coordinates.
; Restore PPU address latch, nametable bits and X/Y scroll.
; IRQ entry immediately returns; no game-specific IRQ service is established here.
; Write MMC3 registers zero through five from pending CHR values. These are CHR bank registers, not effective PRG execution banks.
; Entries choose zero or one for MMC3 mirroring control and return after the shared hardware-write tail.
; Write the caller's mirroring value to MMC3 and return. The adjacent audio initializer clears DMC level, channel IDs, register shadows and music/effect state before shared setup.
; Reset channel state, DMC output and register shadows before stopping both playback groups.
; Preserve caller X/Y, dispatch sound ID A through the priority allocator, then restore registers and return.
; Restore saved Y/X and return from the effect request.
; Negative IDs stop effects; otherwise compare channel mask and priorities, select stream pointer and allocate available effect voices.
; Preserve flags while storing the selected priority and effect mask; the saved equality result controls continuation.
; OR four effect voice masks into the active effect-channel mask.
; Clear four effect voice countdowns and ownership/priority fields, then restore their default register shadows.

; Reset gate/volume/envelope/duration/pitch fields, initialize this voice's stream stack and read its three-byte pointer/register tuple. Register offset $10 selects the alternate pitch table; timers start at one.

; Restore saved Y/X and return from the music request.

; Finish resetting music register shadows; negative IDs stop playback, otherwise select the header and initialize up to four idle music voices from its encoded count.

; Masks $08/$10 used by the signed nibble and five-bit BIT tests; these are data, not code.

; Store the decoded global audio control byte and resume note decoding.
